text_blocks.snippet: COVID-19 in children can range from asymptomatic or mild infections to severe illness requiring hospitalization. While most children experience mild symptoms, certain factors can increase their risk of severe disease, such as underlying health conditions, weakened immune systems, or being unvaccinated.
snippet_highlighted_words: can range from asymptomatic or mild infections to severe illness requiring hospitalization

list.snippet: Common: Fever, cough, sore throat, and runny nose are frequently reported.
Less Common: Some children may experience fatigue, muscle aches, headache, loss of taste or smell, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Severe: In rare cases, children can develop serious complications like pneumonia, breathing difficulties, or multi-system inflammatory syndrome (MIS-C), which requires immediate medical attention.
Underlying Health Conditions: Children with chronic diseases (heart, lung, nervous system), weakened immune systems, obesity, or diabetes are at higher risk.
Vaccination Status: Unvaccinated children are more vulnerable to severe illness compared to those who are fully vaccinated.
Prematurity: Babies born prematurely may also be at increased risk.

list.title: Vaccination:
list.snippet: Vaccination is the most effective way to protect children from severe illness and complications.

list.title: Social Distancing:
list.snippet: Maintaining distance from others, especially during periods of high transmission, can help reduce the spread of the virus.

list.title: Masking:
list.snippet: Wearing masks, especially indoors and in crowded settings, can help prevent the transmission of respiratory droplets.

list.title: Hand Hygiene:
list.snippet: Frequent handwashing with soap and water or using hand sanitizer can reduce the risk of infection.

list.title: Avoiding Close Contact:
list.snippet: Avoiding close contact with individuals who are sick can also help prevent the spread of COVID-19.
